$schema-comment: Claude Code plugin hook manifest. The Stop event fires once per assistant response — every turn end. The hook calls `bettermemory audit-turn`, which reads the hook's stdin JSON (session_id + transcript_path), runs `probe_for_miss` over the pool `memory_search` would have built for that message (`handlers.search.resolve_search_pool`) — above the FTS index threshold a capped, query-biased prefilter slice, not the whole store; and drawn with the raw user message rather than the query the model would have typed, so it matches production's mechanism, not necessarily production's rows — and writes `turn_audited` / `search_miss` events to the on-disk event log. The CLI is designed to always exit 0; the trailing `|| true` is belt-and-suspenders so a uvx network failure, an older PyPI version that doesn't yet have the subcommand, or any other unexpected shape never surfaces as a hook error banner in Claude Code. Losing one turn of telemetry is preferable to interrupting the user.
$schema-comment-session-start: The SessionStart event fires when a conversation opens. Its stdout — uniquely, along with UserPromptSubmit — is injected verbatim into the model's context, which is the entire point: `bettermemory session-start` prints the per-scope memory counts for the current repository, so a fresh session begins already knowing what is stored instead of spending a `memory_scope_overview` tool call to find out (or, far more often, never finding out, because retrieval is opt-in and, between prompts the recall hook's high bar doesn't fire on, nothing prompts it). The subcommand reads the FTS index only, never memory bodies — except under `[behavior] standing_tier = true` (default off), where it also parses the caller-scoped `ambient` files the index names, appends in full the ones the index labels local and the verdict reads fresh (newest-verified first, ~1 KB whole-memory-truncation budget), points at the rest by id, scopes and provenance label (never the body), and collapses the stale local ones to a single verify-to-restore-delivery line: the standing tier is the one surface that delivers without being asked, because opt-in retrieval cannot serve knowledge whose trigger condition is not knowing you need it. Flag on or off, it records NO event and opens NO session (a recorded row would become the anchor `hook._latest_in_process_session` attributes the next turn audit against — it skips only `triggered_from` values in `hook._OUT_OF_PROCESS_TRIGGERS`), prints nothing when the store is empty or the index cannot be trusted, and always exits 0. MATCHER DELIBERATELY OMITTED: per the Claude Code hooks reference an omitted matcher means 'match all', and all five SessionStart matchers — startup, resume, clear, compact, fork — want the hint. `clear` and `compact` in particular have just discarded the context this block supplies, which is exactly when re-injecting it is most valuable. Pinning the five by name would be equivalent today and silently stop firing on a sixth. Timeout is 20s rather than the Stop hook's 30 because this one blocks session open, where latency is visible.
$schema-comment-prompt-recall: The UserPromptSubmit event fires when the user submits a prompt, before the model sees it; stdout on exit 0 is injected into the model's context (the same channel SessionStart uses). `bettermemory prompt-recall` reads the hook's stdin JSON (`session_id`, `prompt`) and runs the SAME probe the Stop hook's audit-turn runs — `hook._probe_message`: production's search pool, production's ranking inputs, the v1 threshold rule, all four shields. Where that probe would later have flagged the turn a silent miss, this hook instead prints a one-hit pointer block (memory id + scopes + query-biased snippet, never a body — the verify-before-relying read path stays on memory_show) and records a `prompt_recall` event. The event is a member of `audit._RETRIEVAL_EVENT_KINDS`, so the Stop hook's audit of the same turn reports `ok` rather than re-flagging a delivery as a miss, and a second injection inside the attribution window self-suppresses. The predicate fires on two lanes (6.2.0): the classic would-be silent miss (~2% of audited turns historically, docs/eval-results.md) and, under `[behavior] recall_in_project` (default on), the project cohort the audit deliberately declines to flag — the caller stands inside the repo the top hit was written from, where memory-resident facts are exactly what the open source tree cannot serve. The don't-pollute-generic-answers stance is enforced by the bar and shields, not by opt-in; `[behavior] prompt_recall = false` turns the hook into a guaranteed no-op, and with `telemetry.enabled = false` it refuses to inject rather than inject off the books. MATCHER DELIBERATELY OMITTED: UserPromptSubmit defines no matcher values, and an omitted matcher means 'match all'. Timeout is 10s, the tightest of the three hooks, because this one sits between the user pressing enter and the model starting — the common path (no injection) exits in well under a second, and losing one recall beats delaying every prompt.
